title: Scientists Grow Potatoes in Moon Soil
paragraphs: Boil 'em, mash 'em, eat 'em on ... the moon?
Full of nutrients, potatoes are a favorite here on Earth. But they could perhaps help feed astronauts living on the moon one day.
Scientists in the US have now taken a step toward making that possible by growing potatoes in special soil made to be similar to the soil on the moon.
This could help astronauts grow their own food if people live on the moon in the future.
But growing potatoes in moon soil isn't easy. Unlike Earth's soil, moon soil has very little organic material, which plants need to grow well.
So researchers at Oregon State University wanted to find out if adding compost could help.
Compost is made from old plants and other natural waste, and it has the nutrients that help plants grow.
The researchers used compost made with the help of earthworms. They mixed different amounts of it into the moon-like soil and planted potatoes.
And the results were encouraging. Potato plants grown in soil with 30% compost grew just as well as potato plants grown in normal Earth soil.
However, without compost, the potato plants were much smaller and had weak roots. Adding smaller amounts of compost helped, but the plants still didn't grow as well as those grown with 30% compost.
The potatoes were also found to be safe to eat.

NASA hopes to have people living and working on the moon by the early 2030s, and growing food there could mean fewer supplies need to come from Earth. Astronauts could take a small amount of compost to the moon, and make more using leftover food and plants.
This may be one small step for potatoes, but it's one giant leap for humans being able to live away from the Earth!
